scenes.heading: Persuasive writing
scenes.sub: Pick a side, prove it, and answer the other side
scenes.say: In a persuasive task, you get a statement and you have to win the reader over. Markers want a clear side, strong reasons explained well, and a calm, confident voice. Let's build one.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A good captain explains the game plan, not just "we'll win"
scenes.science: A persuasive writer explains reasons, not just "I'm right"
scenes.breaks: a team already wants to win; your reader may start out disagreeing with you.
scenes.say: Think of a team captain. Shouting we'll win doesn't help. Explaining the plan does. Persuasive writing is the same: saying you're right isn't enough. You have to explain why.

scenes.heading: The structure
scenes.say: Here's the structure. An introduction with a clear position. Two body paragraphs, each one reason. A rebuttal that answers the other side. Then a conclusion that restates your position and finishes strongly.

scenes.heading: PEEL paragraphs
scenes.say: Build each body paragraph with PEEL. Point: your reason. Evidence: an example. Explain: why that example supports your point. Link: tie it back to your position. Explain is the step students skip most, and it's where the persuading happens.

scenes.heading: What is missing?
scenes.question: "Uniforms save families money. A set can be worn every school day. That is why uniforms should stay."
lines: No reason why it saves money
scenes.say: What's missing here? Point: uniforms save money. Evidence: a set is worn every day. Link: so they should stay. But nothing explains why that saves money. The missing part is Explain.

scenes.heading: Persuade, don't shout
scenes.say: Some habits weaken you: insulting the other side, made-up statistics, and cramming in ten techniques. Stay calm and confident, use believable examples, and pick two or three techniques like rhetorical questions or inclusive language.

points: Choose one side and keep to it
scenes.say: Quick recap. Choose a side and keep to it. Use PEEL for every body paragraph. Answer the other side fairly. And conclude without adding new reasons. Now try the practice questions!
